text: Neutrophils are more abundant in the human body than any other type of white blood cell. In addition to possessing phagocytic capabilities, neutrophils release proteases that aid in breaking down cellular debris from EIMD. They also secrete cytolytic and cytotoxic substances that can exacerbate damage to injured muscle and inflict damage to healthy neighboring tissues (277). Hence, their primary role in skeletal muscle is likely confined to myolysis and other facets associated with the removal of cellular debris as opposed to the regeneration of contractile tissue.
book: Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy
